# The in-flight update registry reports a scope the payload no longer has

## Context

Found while investigating `#17980`. **It is not that ticket's cure** — `#17980` was cured separately by `#17999` and is closed — and, per cross-family review, this ticket originally over-claimed what its evidence supports. **Amended below to the defect that is actually witnessed.**

## The Problem

`Neo.manager.VDomUpdate`'s in-flight registry records a component's update depth **once**, when the cycle opens. The payload is built from `component.updateDepth` read **live**, after a macrotask yield. Nothing reconciles the two.

```javascript
// src/mixin/VdomLifecycle.mjs — executeVdomUpdate
me.isVdomUpdating = true;
VDomUpdate.registerInFlightUpdate(me.id, me.updateDepth);   // recorded HERE
await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 1));       // ← the window
// ...
depths.set(componentId, component.updateDepth);             // read LIVE, HERE
```

`Component#show()` writes into exactly that window, correctly — a floating widget mounting into its parent needs the full tree:

```javascript
me.parent.updateDepth = -1;
me.parent.update()
```

**So the registry reports a scope the payload no longer has.** `getInFlightUpdateDepth` answers `1` while the payload is being built at `-1`. Measured in a real browser on a real `tab.header.Toolbar`:

```
[cycle2 open] updating=true  live=1   registered=1
[ESCALATED]   live=-1        registered=1     ← disagreement
```

Reaching it needs a **second** cycle: `getVdomUpdatePayload` resets the depth by writing `_updateDepth` directly, so a component that has ever been at `-1` stays there until one payload is collected. First-cycle-only reasoning concludes the window is unreachable.

## What this ticket claims — and what it deliberately does NOT

**Claimed and witnessed:** the in-flight registry is incoherent with the payload during that window. `isParentUpdating` and `hasUpdateCollision` consult the registry, so any consumer of the collision contract is answered from a stale value.

**NOT claimed:** that this produces a second overlapping flight or duplicate DOM. I hypothesised that chain and **measured that it does not occur** — with the hook disabled the sibling is still queued, because something further down absorbs it. That absorber is unidentified. The duplicate-DOM defect was `#17980`, cured by `#17999`.

This narrowing is the result of @neo-gpt-emmy's review, which correctly observed that I had disclosed the gap in the spec and then left the causal claim standing in the ticket, the PR body and the commit messages. **A registry-coherence defect is what the evidence supports.**

## The Architectural Reality

`beforeSetUpdateDepth` makes depth **monotonic with `-1` absorbing**:

```javascript
return oldValue === -1 || value === -1 ? -1 : Math.max(value, oldValue)
```

Deliberate and load-bearing. **Freezing the depth for the in-flight cycle — the obvious fix — would drop a mounting widget out of the payload meant to carry it**, and was flagged by the operator as a severe-regression risk on this surface.

## The Fix

Widen the **record**, never the payload. `VDomUpdate.escalateInFlightUpdate(ownerId, depth)` updates the recorded depth for a component already in flight, mirroring the same monotonic contract, called from an `afterSetUpdateDepth` hook.

Directional safety: **this can only widen what the collision check knows.** Being wrong costs serialization; it can never drop a subtree. `getVdomUpdatePayload` resets by writing `_updateDepth` directly and so never reaches the hook — a collection reset cannot narrow an open flight.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `getInFlightUpdateDepth` reports the same scope the payload is built from, for the whole window between escalation and settlement
- [ ] `show()` still escalates the payload to `-1` — asserted at unit **and** component tier; narrowing it is the regression this must not cause
- [ ] The record only ever widens: `-1` absorbs, otherwise `Math.max`; a component with no in-flight entry never gains one
- [ ] A reset written during collection (`_updateDepth`, bypassing the setter) cannot narrow an open flight
- [ ] Every retained arm is **mutation-proven** — red without the hook, green with it
- [ ] **No arm is retained that passes with the hook disabled**, and no assertion on registry values is labelled behavioural

## Out of Scope

- **`#17980`'s duplication.** Cured by `#17999`; this does not address it and must not be described as if it does.
- Identifying what absorbs the sibling write downstream of the collision check. Real, unowned, and not required for registry coherence.
- Both naive apply-layer id guards in `DeltaUpdates` — falsified and recorded on `#17980`.

## Avoided Traps

- **Freezing the in-flight depth.** Correct-looking, severe regression: `show()` mounts floating widgets through that escalation.
- **Keeping a causal claim the evidence does not carry.** The original body asserted a second flight and duplicate DOM. I had already measured that it does not occur and disclosed it *in the spec file only* — the claim survived everywhere else. That is what this amendment removes.
- **Calling a registry-value assertion a behavioural arm.** A label is not a witness.
